description: Ex-RAF VV211, one of first three IAF jet fighters (Aircraft Testing Unit Kanpur, Nov 1948), delivered as VT-CXJ. Wore training number T-27 for decades at AFTC gate; identified 2005 and repainted VT-CXJ/HB546 with Chakra markings and No.7 Sqn Battle Axe. Displayed at right end of AFTC parade ground on cradle support. Source WoI (page updated Sep 2025), BR.
Pole-mounted at AFTC parade ground since 2005 with mannequins in cockpit, engine removed. Source WoI, BR.
Pole-mounted at AFTC parade ground since 2005, opposite side to IX502, mannequins in cockpit. Source WoI, BR.
c/n T.009. Third AFTC HT-2, retained as ground instructional airframe, not seen by WoI. Source WoI, BR.

Type 74, only surviving IAF MiG-21F-13, flown by Wg Cdr Wollen in the 1965 war. Sectioned cutaway instructional airframe with illuminated plexiglass panels, kept in a shed. Source WoI (page updated Sep 2025), BR.
Type 77 ground instructional airframe, was in taxiable/engine-run condition; formerly desert camouflage with MOFTU badge, now standard grey. Source WoI, BR.
Type 77 ground instructional airframe in natural metal, stored outside main hangar. Source WoI.
Last flown June 2000 (No.224 Sqn), ground instructional airframe with serviceable engine, repainted grey 2004-05. Source WoI, BR.
Retired from GI role, now a parade-ground guardian on the left flank. Source WoI, BR.
Second AFTC Gnat, fully de-skinned cutaway fuselage (structure painted yellow) with wings sectioned on a table in the same shed as BC817; identity unknown. Source WoI (updated Sep 2025).

Ex-Hakimpet, received early 2005, pole-mounted at parade ground with mannequins. BR notes c/n 3H-1507 and that the serial W1767 was later re-used on replacement airframe 3H-1903; identity of the displayed airframe per BR is the Srs XIX replacement. Source WoI (updated Sep 2025), BR.
c/n 3H-1516, delivered Feb 1976. Pole-mounted at AFTC parade ground since 2005, diverging from W1767. Source WoI, BR.
c/n 1701, early Chetak used for helicopter maintenance training at AFTC. Source WoI, BR.
Instructional airframe at AFTC, seen on Google Earth imagery; not photographed by WoI. Source WoI, BR.
